messages:
maria: Quick heads-up — starting onboarding for aurora-70b-mqa-v2. Weights are uploaded to s3://redwood-models/aurora/70b/mqa-v2/, tokenizer artifacts in s3://redwood-models/aurora/70b/tokenizer/. Need a fast compatibility pass: RoPE scaling sanity, sliding-window/KV TTL behavior, and attention impl validation. Any red flags before I open the canary? :eyes:

kai: @maria copy. I'll kick off a tokenizer smoke + RoPE-scale probe. Do you have a representative prompt set (long/short) or should I reuse the default onboard prompts?

maria: Use onboard prompts + the new long-form test (max 32k tokens spread across a conversation). Also include some code-heavy prompts — tokenizer sometimes splits weirdly.

kai: Got it. Starting tokenization check now. If tokenizer.eos_id != 50256 we should flag. Will report results in ~10m.

alex: Re: attention impl — last time a 70b MQA variant hit weird softmax overflow on older kernels. If you see large logits or nan in attention scores, stop and ping @eng-runtime. Also confirm rotary base scaling and rope_interp config.

maria: Noted. The model config includes: 
```
model_type: autoregressive
attention: flash_attention_v2
rope: {base: 10000, scale: 1.5, interp: linear}
gqa: enabled
sliding_window: {enabled: true, window_size: 2048, stride: 512, ttl_ms: 1200}
```
Is that compatible with current runtime?

jeff: flash_attention_v2 should be OK on our 8xA100 pools but double-check on the dedicated-nvlink lane. GQA enabled + MQA is fine but watch KV layout differences — run a kv-roundtrip test to ensure cache hit parity.

kai: Tokenizer smoke done: small differences in eos id mapping — tokenizer.json shows eos=220, not 50256. That explains some anchor differences. I pushed a quick mapping patch to the staging tokenizer bundle (sha: a1b2c3).

maria: Hmm — mapping patch makes sense. Would that break previously served variants? We need fallback: if eos mismatch, rewrite token stream on the fly.

sara: For graceful rollout, suggest config-level fallback: 
```
tokenizer_fallbacks: ["eos_map_v1","eos_map_50256"]
```
Runtime will attempt the first, then fallback without failing the request. Low-risk.

alex: I ran a RoPE scale probe (script: scripts/rope_probe.py) against the canary weights. Output: 
```
rope_probe summary: scale=1.5 -> relative perplexity delta +0.3% (within noise). no nan/inf in attention. rotary angles look OK.
```
No immediate concerns.

kai: KV-roundtrip test passed for short sequences. For the long-form test I saw occasional cache miss spikes when sliding_window.ttl_ms < average token latency. Increasing ttl_ms to 2500ms reduces misses.

infra-bot: deploy-checklist status: tokenizer-smoke=pass, rope-probe=pass, kv-roundtrip=partial, long-window-stress=running

maria: Thanks. Action items: 1) bump sliding_window.ttl_ms to 2500 for canary, 2) include tokenizer_fallbacks config, 3) add eos mapping to tokenizer bundle and tag v2, 4) run one controlled canary with 5% traffic. Anyone want to own the canary run?

jeff: I can own the canary run today. I'll coordinate with oncall to watch latency SLO and error rates.

kai: I'll redo the long-form run after ttl bump and post logs. If we still see cache chatter, we can try a smaller stride (384).

sara: I'll prepare the config PR with fallback and ttl bump. Small note: add a rollout flag so we can auto-fallback to 13b if errors spike.

maria: Perfect. If jeff starts the canary, I'll monitor qualitative output for hallucination regressions and tokenizer artifacts. We should be able to decide within 2 hours. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Reminder — file an incident if error-rate > 3% or p95 latency increase > 40% for more than 5 minutes.

kai: Logging snippets I'll attach after the run: tokenizer diffs, rope angles, and attention score histograms.

maria: Thanks team. Leaving this thread open for async updates. If anyone sees anything blocking, ping me directly.
